text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.1% today as oil prices climbed on escalating Middle East tensions—WTI crude hit its highest level since July following fresh U.S. strikes against Iran. The stock has also gained 4.3% over the past two weeks, tracking alongside broader crude strength and the unfolding geopolitical situation that's lifted prices from around $130 at the end of August to nearly $84 per barrel today.

The Venezuela oil deal announced this week—securing U.S. access to 65 billion barrels through a new concession agreement—adds a longer-term tailwind for large oil producers. While the near-term impact remains uncertain, the combination of tighter Middle East supply concerns and the prospect of additional crude reserves moving into Western hands is supporting crude prices and, by extension, energy stocks like this one.
